lt-0iED.title: Km marker: blue, L-shaped, 45° to the road
lt-0iED.summary: All three Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker, but here it is L-shaped and sits at a 45° angle to the road.

differs.how: Marker sits at a different angle to the road
Marker sits at a different angle to the road

lt-1lsP.title: Sign: bilingual with Polish
lt-1lsP.summary: Rare bilingual signs with Polish in a small area in the southeast. Not common, but it gets you a close guess if the rest looks clearly Lithuanian.

lt-3bOZ.title: Flag: knight on horseback, dark red
lt-3bOZ.summary: A historical flag showing a mounted knight on a dark red background, seen on private and public buildings.

lt-5FSb.title: Sign: street word "gatvė", short "g."
lt-5FSb.summary: The word for street is gatvė, often shortened to g. It is almost unique to this country, though Riga rarely has "gat.".

lt-5P5C.title: Language: Ą Ę Į Ų, dotted Ė, Y
lt-5P5C.summary: A Baltic language, closely related to Latvian. Hooked vowels Ą Ę Į Ų, the dotted Ė and the letter Y are unique to it. Estonian looks very different.

differs.how: Estonian is not Baltic and looks very different

lt-8k76.title: Vegetation: more open, less forest
lt-8k76.summary: Less forest than the other Baltic countries, so the land looks more open and farmed. It varies by round, so use with caution.

lt-FSkc.title: Pole: metal pole tags in the east
lt-FSkc.summary: Metal tags on poles are mostly found in the eastern part of the country.

lt-GkfG.title: Sign: blue direction sign
lt-GkfG.summary: Blue direction signs with white text. The arrowhead has a vertical back, as in Estonia, while Latvia's arrow is more stylised.

differs.how: Latvian arrow is more stylised

lt-N6PY.title: Pole: square concrete with diagonal brace
lt-N6PY.summary: Square concrete poles, often with a diagonal support beam. Seen sometimes in Estonia and rarely in Latvia, but most common here.

lt-NpdU.title: Google car: red Gen 4
lt-NpdU.summary: A red Gen 4 car. Latvia and a few other European countries have it too, but Estonia does not.

differs.how: Estonia has no red Gen 4 car

lt-RWCn.title: Pole: short rods or trident-style insulators
lt-RWCn.summary: Poletops often have short horizontal rods holding the insulators, or insulators in a trident shape: one on top, two at each side. Other post-Soviet countries have these too.

lt-SYjp.title: Bollard: wedge, orange front, white back
lt-SYjp.summary: Wedge-shaped bollard with a rectangular orange reflector on the front and a white one on the back. A thinner version also exists.

differs.how: Estonian bollards look different
Latvian bollards look different

lt-Uc6g.title: Chevron: white with red arrows, red edge
lt-Uc6g.summary: White chevrons with red arrows. The small single ones usually have a red outline on the edge. Latvia and Poland use the same without the outline, while Estonia, Russia and Ukraine use red with white arrows.

differs.how: Estonian chevrons are red with white arrows
Russian chevrons are red with white arrows
Ukrainian chevrons are red with white arrows

lt-YZaL.title: Google car: black Gen 4
lt-YZaL.summary: A black Gen 4 car. Latvia and a few other European countries have it too, but Estonia does not.

differs.how: Estonia has no black Gen 4 car

lt-evbw.title: Houses: red wooden Scandinavian-style
lt-evbw.summary: On the sand spit you also see wooden, often red, houses that look Scandinavian.

lt-fAPZ.title: Google car: random small blurs in Gen 3
lt-fAPZ.summary: In older Gen 3 coverage, small random blurs cover parts of the image, often direction signs. They look like face or plate blurs. Neighbouring Kaliningrad has them too; Estonia and Latvia usually don't.

differs.how: Random blurs are not typical there
Random blurs are not typical there

lt-ggZt.title: Plate: long white with blue EU strip
lt-ggZt.summary: Long white plates with the standard blue European strip on the left.

lt-koWn.title: Guardrail: A-type with orange reflectors
lt-koWn.summary: Normal A-type guardrail with orange reflectors.

differs.how: Estonian guardrails have no reflectors
Latvian guardrail reflectors are red or white

lt-lm-2997.title: Sign: pedestrian, chunky figure, vivid blue
lt-lm-2997.summary: Among 3-stripe pedestrian signs, rule out Estonia (detailed figure) and Russia (yellow borders). The figure here is a bit fatter in the torso than Ukraine's, and the blue is more vivid.

differs.how: Ukrainian figure is slimmer, blue less vivid
Estonian figure is more detailed
Russian signs have yellow borders

lt-lm-740357.title: House numbers: very big with curvy lines
lt-lm-740357.summary: House numbers are very large, with curvy lines above and below the digits.

lt-lm-740358.title: Street sign: white, black text, black frame
lt-lm-740358.summary: Street signs are white with black text inside a black frame. The house number has the same design and often sits next to the street name.

lt-mtfw.title: Landscape: flat, hills only southeast and west
lt-mtfw.summary: Fairly flat with no hills over 300 metres. The biggest hills are in the southeast, with some in the central west.

lt-nVmi.title: Houses: light brick
lt-nVmi.summary: Mostly light-coloured brick buildings with fairly steep corrugated metal roofs. Wooden houses are fairly common but less than in Estonia, and pastel stone buildings appear in newer suburbs.

differs.how: Estonia has even more wooden buildings

lt-oTsA.title: Landscape: sand spit, pines, windswept trees
lt-oTsA.summary: A long thin sand-dune spit. The main road runs roughly north to south with Gen 4 coverage, surrounded by forest of pines, often slightly windswept.

lt-q5r2.title: Sign: thin red border, thin white outline
lt-q5r2.summary: Warning and speed signs have a fairly thin red border with a thin white outline around it. Each Baltic country has a slightly different border.

lt-sIcK.title: Sign: bus stop, bus with four windows
lt-sIcK.summary: Bus stop sign showing a bus with four windows, unlike Latvia's five. Estonia's sign is the same as here.

differs.how: Latvian bus has five windows

lt-tXGz.title: Sign: pedestrian, 3 stripes, simple figure
lt-tXGz.summary: Pedestrian crossing sign with 3 stripes and a fairly simple figure. Russia and Ukraine have the same design, while Estonia has a more detailed figure.

differs.how: Estonian figure is more detailed
Latvian signs have 5 stripes
